correctness.rationale: Inclusion-exclusion yields S(n,5)=G_r((n−r)/2)−(2^(2n−3)+2^(n−2))/3. For nonzero h∈Z_2, the first summand in 120(G_r(t+h)−G_r(t)) has valuation v2(h)+3, the second v2(h)+4; dividing by 120 gives v2(G_r(t+h)−G_r(t))=v2(h). The induced finite maps are bijections, giving once per parity, while the correction has exactly valuation n−2 and vanishes at n≥k+2. The mod-two 1100 pattern excludes odd periods, the isometry excludes shorter even periods, and at n=k+1 the period shift fails for k≥4. All domains and edge exponents are covered. A standalone recurrence-based verifier checked exponents 1–12; finite checks do not replace the proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Kwong does cover the minimal-period conclusion and that subclaim is explicitly prior work. Special-index difference valuations do not give full parity-class bijectivity or earliest onset.

value.rationale: This is a natural and complete fixed-column modular distribution invariant for a classical combinatorial sequence; it sharpens known eventual periodicity and fifth-column valuation analysis to exact equal output fibers at every precision, one-per-parity uniqueness, and a sharp transient boundary. Column five is the first fixed positive column whose tail can achieve full uniform 2-power residue support, unlike columns one through four already modulo four. The arithmetic isometry supplies a reusable conceptual explanation rather than a new tabulation or weak period corollary.
